causal_boundary.not_supported: The public Git history does not identify the exact code commit or memory-database bytes used for the paper's Table-3 runs. Therefore the paper-level 'same memory' comparison must not be upgraded to an exact reproducible fixed-snapshot claim solely from the repository.
causal_boundary.supported: The authors now expose an official implementation and a read-only memory mode, but the public revision and memory snapshots are not provenance-bound to the May-8 paper evaluation.

observations.claim: The repository README identifies air-embodied-brain/MemCompiler as the official implementation of arXiv:2605.07594 and supports ScienceWorld.

Public main history starts with an 'Initial release' commit d09a5462f5af6f19478c3f8dedb0b9c4d36dac1a dated 2026-05-23, after the arXiv record dated 2026-05-08; current inspected main revision ec5a5792873dc84785036a69a73d1cf2c669c0f9 is dated 2026-05-29.

At both initial release and current inspected main, tasks/run_manager_executor_scienceworld.py sets UPDATE_MEMORY=True by default. The runner also has a read-only Memcompiler branch when UPDATE_MEMORY=False.
The current trained-model evaluation script also sets UPDATE_MEMORY=True and points ScienceWorld memory to a local .db_eval.../memcompiler path.
Repository .gitignore excludes output*/ and .db*/; no GitHub releases are published. Thus the evaluated memory database/snapshot bytes are not versioned on the inspected public repository surface.

protocol_implication: For a fixed-memory ablation handoff, bind each condition to the exact implementation revision, initial memory snapshot digest, candidate-universe digest, update policy, and non-memory control digest. A paper statement that conditions use the same bank is useful causal evidence, but public replay identity remains unresolved until the bank bytes and evaluated revision are bound.
